stem:
Meera lives near a busy road in Jaipur. Her family burns waste plastic in the courtyard, and nearby trees are being cut to build shops. Her teacher says such human actions threaten life on Earth.

Which statement best explains how these actions create major threats to life?

options.text: Burning fuels and waste releases greenhouse gases that trap heat, while cutting trees destroys habitats and disturbs the balance of living and non-living systems.
Burning waste and cutting trees are separate small problems, so they cannot disturb the balance that supports life on Earth.
Only factories in big cities release greenhouse gases, so actions at home like burning waste do not threaten life.
The disturbed balance of Earth systems comes first, and this is what causes human activities like burning fuels and cutting trees.

teacher.key_rationale: Human actions such as burning fossil fuels and waste release greenhouse gases that trap heat, and habitat destruction and pollution disturb the balance of living and non-living systems that supports life; option A states this causal chain correctly. B wrongly treats the threats as unrelated, C wrongly restricts the cause to factories, and D reverses the cause-and-effect relationship.
